subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram group: cross-agent sessions_list visibility mismatch causes one-way sessions_send failure

question: Should same-Telegram-group cross-agent sessions become symmetrically visible/sendable under the current session visibility model, or should cross-agent sends wait for a broader per-capability or per-agent authorization contract?
rationale: The issue points at a real session-delivery problem, but the likely fixes change the boundary between message delivery, session listing, transcript access, and same-group trust.

options.title: Choose the broader contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open, settle the related per-capability/per-agent A2A semantics, then implement the Telegram proof case against that contract.

options.title: Approve a narrow send-only exception
options.body: Allow `sessions_send` to rely on explicit A2A policy while keeping list, history, and status visibility-gated, with live Telegram A/B proof and regression tests.

options.title: Treat same group as not enough
options.body: Document that same Telegram group membership does not imply cross-agent access and require the existing broad visibility plus A2A configuration until a new contract lands.

recommendation.title: Choose the broader contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, settle the related per-capability/per-agent A2A semantics, then implement the Telegram proof case against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history is closest to the session-tool security scoping and shared access-helper boundary this decision would change.
